readerTitle: How many months can you survive?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (식당, 소프트웨어 스타트업) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 런웨이는 오늘의 손실로 나눈 숫자가 아니라, 앞으로의 순소진액으로 계산하고 대응에 필요한 시간을 뺀 '결정 마감일'이다.
misconception: 통장 잔고를 이번 달 손실로 나누면 버틸 수 있는 기간이 나온다. 그 기간이 끝날 때까지는 움직이지 않아도 된다.

sources.text: 재무관리의 표준 개념 (총소진액·순소진액, 런웨이 = 현금 ÷ 월 순소진액)

factChecks.note: 결정 마감일: 런웨이 4.3개월 − 대응 준비 3개월(가정) = 약 1.3개월. 3개월은 설명용 가정이며 실제 대응 기간은 사업마다 다릅니다.
소프트웨어 계산: $600,000 ÷ $50,000 = 12개월. 두 명 채용 시 $600,000 ÷ $70,000 = 8.57개월, 투자 유치 6개월(가정)을 빼면 약 2.6개월. 한 명 채용 시 $600,000 ÷ $60,000 = 10개월, 6개월을 빼면 4개월. 투자 유치 기간 6개월은 실제 통계가 아닌 시나리오 가정입니다.

cards.title: How many months can you survive?
body: A neighborhood restaurant has $90,000 in the bank. It has lost money for three months straight.
The owner divides cash by last month's loss and feels calm. The answer she gets depends on which number she divides by, and the honest one is much smaller.

image.label: Restaurant cash register with a shrinking stack of bills
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 저녁 영업 중인 작은 식당 카운터. 계산대 옆에 지폐 더미가 있고, 벽 달력의 몇 장이 날아가는 모션. 실제 브랜드나 로고 없음.

cards.title: How long until the cash runs out?
body: Each month the restaurant takes in $50,000 and pays out $65,000. It has $90,000 in cash.
Starting this month, a new chef adds $6,000 a month in pay. If nothing else changes, how many months does the cash last?

options.feedback: That's $90,000 ÷ $15,000, today's loss. It ignores a cost you already know is coming, so it promises two extra months that don't exist.
Right. With the chef, $21,000 more goes out than comes in each month. $90,000 ÷ $21,000 is about 4.3 months.
That's the answer if sales stopped completely. It's a useful worst case, but customers still pay $50,000 a month.

cards.title: Follow one month of cash.
body: One known cost cut the time left from 6 months to about **4.3**. Nothing went wrong. The owner just planned with last month's number.

cards.title: Burn rate and runway
body: **Burn rate** is how fast cash leaves. *Gross burn* is everything you pay out in a month. *Net burn* is cash out minus cash in.
**Runway** is how many months your cash lasts: cash in the bank ÷ net burn. Use cash, not profit. Profit can look fine while cash drains away.
The twist: use the burn you expect in the coming months, not the one you saw last month.

cards.title: Your real deadline comes earlier.
body: Fixing a cash problem takes time. Getting a loan, raising prices, renegotiating rent or giving notice on a lease can each take months.
Say the owner needs about three months to act. With 4.3 months of runway, she has roughly **one month** to decide. Runway minus time to act is your decision date.

image.label: Timeline: 4.3 months of runway, last 3 shaded as time to act
image.brief: 가로 타임라인 인포그래픽. 0에서 4.3개월까지 막대. 마지막 3개월 구간은 주황색으로 'Time to act', 앞쪽 약 1개월 끝에 깃발 'Decision date'. 깔끔한 플랫 스타일.

cards.title: One month can fool you.
body: Burn moves. A beach café burns cash all winter and earns it back in summer. A good December can hide a weak quarter.
Average net burn over several months, then adjust for changes you already know: a hire, a rent increase, a slow season. Recheck it every month.
cards.softwareNote: Startups often track runway monthly because burn grows with each hire. A team of ten can burn far faster than a team of five, even with rising revenue.

cards.title: Cutting costs can shorten runway.
body: Runway is a forecast, not a fact. Cash in the bank may already be owed: taxes, supplier bills, customer deposits. Count only what's truly free.
And cuts work on net burn, not gross burn. If the $6,000 chef brings in $8,000 of extra sales, letting him go raises the burn. Ask what each cost earns before cutting it.

cards.title: Now it's a software startup.
body: Your app business has $600,000 in cash and burns $50,000 a month, so 12 months of runway. You expect raising new money to take about six months.
You want two engineers at $10,000 a month each. What do you do?

options.feedback: Runway drops to about 8.6 months. You'd need to start raising in about 2.5 months, likely before the new hires show results.
You keep 12 months, but slower progress can make the raise harder. Saving runway isn't the same as using it well.

options.text: Hire one now, and set a date to start raising
options.feedback: Runway falls to 10 months, leaving four before you must start raising. You buy progress and keep a clear decision date.

cards.title: Runway is cash ÷ the burn that's coming, minus the time you need to act.
body: Last month's loss tells you the past. Runway is about the months ahead, and your decision date arrives before the money runs out.
**Try it today:** divide your cash by your average net cash out over the last three months. Adjust for changes you know are coming. Then mark your decision date.
